observations: Photo 0: Top view of a silver laptop with black keyboard, trackpad, and closed screen. The left side of the palm rest has a blue Intel sticker. The laptop is open at a wide angle, showing the hinge design.

Photo 1: Bottom view of the same laptop, showing the back of the lid and base. The HP logo is visible on the lid. The base has a vented area and a small label with a barcode and Intel logo. The hinge is visible and appears to be a 360-degree rotating type.
Photo 2: Close-up of the Intel sticker on the palm rest. It reads 'Intel CORE i7 vPro 8th Gen'. The sticker is holographic blue and white. The trackpad and part of the keyboard are visible below it.
The laptop appears to be a 2-in-1 convertible model due to the 360-degree hinge visible in photo 1.
The screen is off in photo 0, reflecting light. No visible damage to the screen or keyboard from these angles.

Video showing the screen displaying a clear image.

response.reason: The item is identifiable as an HP 2-in-1 convertible laptop with an Intel Core i7 vPro 8th Gen processor. However, the seller claims the motherboard is bad, which cannot be verified from the photos. Without proof of functionality of the screen, keyboard, trackpad, battery, or internal components, the item cannot be priced accurately. The risk of non-functionality due to the faulty motherboard is too high to assign a price without further evidence.
